- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a price spike (e.g., >70.5), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to offset momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model consistently underestimates in the 10–15 day horizon; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for that window to align with mean reversion bias.  
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive (e.g., +0.3 to -0.1), model fails to adjust; apply a 1–2% upward correction in the next 3–5 days.
